I wanted to discuss the future of ASK.
Hicham wants to develop new branches.
Two arrogant guys showed up.
Darling, it is his money after all.
Yes, but it affects our agency!
They want to do image consulting!
Honestly, where are we heading now?
He will want to do everything together.
He will be less present at ASK.
He should appoint a Managing Director.
Someone who knows the company well!
Mathias is doing yoga with his wife.
Yoga relaxes me a lot, truly.
It is important to be together, darling.

examples.text: Cette agence ne représente que des stars.

meanings.note: une agence artistique = a talent agency

examples.text: Ça va? Oui, ça va bien.
examples.trans: How are you? Yes, I'm fine.

meanings.note: aller + infinitive: tu vas l'agacer = you're going to annoy her
ça va? = how are you? / are you okay?

examples.text: Après, elles ne peuvent plus s'arrêter.
On mange, et après on part.
examples.trans: We eat, and afterwards we leave.

examples.text: Elles commencent avec un peu de Botox. Après, elles ne peuvent plus s'arrêter.
examples.trans: They start with a bit of Botox. Then they can't stop anymore.

examples.text: Alors tu n'as pas besoin d'argent, finalement.
examples.trans: So you don't need money, after all.

examples.text: Non, je viens d'arriver. Mon père, mais c'est compliqué.
examples.trans: No, I've just arrived. My dad, but it's complicated.

meanings.note: je viens d'arriver = I've just arrived

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.
The future of the agency is secure.
He is thinking about his future.

examples.text: Il s'inquiète pour ton avenir professionnel.
examples.trans: He's worried about your professional future.
You know a lot of people.

examples.text: Tu connais beaucoup de monde dans le cinéma. Tu pourrais m'aider.
examples.trans: You know lots of people in film. You could help me.

meanings.note: beaucoup de + noun, with no article: beaucoup de travail

meanings.en: beaucoup de = a lot of, many

meanings.note: as a masculine noun: pour le bien de = for the good of
as a masculine noun: pour le bien de = for the good of
c'est une belle boîte = it's a great company

examples.text: Ouvre la boîte tout de suite.
La vérité, c'est que mon agence... C'est une belle boîte. Un joyau, envié de tous.
examples.trans: The truth is that my agency... It's a great company. A jewel, envied by all.

meanings.en: branch of a tree or business

examples.trans: Hicham wants to open new branches.

examples.trans: Hicham wants to develop new branches.

meanings.note: before a noun: ce film, cette tête, ces gens
as a pronoun in c'est, ce n'est pas; becomes c' before a vowel

examples.trans: We went back to my place.
Really work on it at home.

examples.text: Ça va, chérie? Tu es en retard.

meanings.note: as a form of address: chéri (to a man), chérie (to a woman)

examples.text: Ça concerne Samuel et c'est important.
examples.trans: It concerns Samuel and it's important.

examples.text: Une dernière chose. Ça concerne Samuel et c'est important.
examples.trans: One last thing. It concerns Samuel and it's important.

meanings.en: to know a person or place
ne rien connaître à = to know nothing about

examples.text: Je lui ai donné un petit conseil pour réussir.
examples.trans: I gave her a little tip to succeed.

examples.text: La plus grande imprésario de Paris.

meanings.note: je n'ai pas de temps; also before a plural adjective: de mauvaises nouvelles

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: the x sounds like z before a vowel

examples.text: Ils sont prêts à en discuter.
examples.trans: They're ready to talk about it.

examples.text: J'ai quelque chose pour se détendre.

meanings.note: First-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are'), the most productive verb class in French. Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Core French verb meaning 'to develop, expand'.

examples.text: Hicham veut développer des nouvelles branches.
examples.trans: Hicham wants to develop new branches.
I was having dinner with Samuel.

examples.text: Bonsoir. Il y a quelques semaines, je dînais avec Samuel.
examples.trans: Good evening. A few weeks ago, I was having dinner with Samuel.

meanings.note: preposition: en vacances, en huit ans
pronoun before the verb: j'en ai assez, je n'en peux plus

examples.text: On a toujours voulu jouer ensemble.
examples.trans: We've always wanted to act together.

meanings.en: as a noun: the whole, a set

meanings.note: pour faire quoi? = to do what?
faire du vélo = to ride a bike, to cycle

falloir.governs: il faut + infinitive, or il faut que + subjunctive

meanings.note: only with the impersonal 'il': il faut
il me faut un stylo = I need a pen

examples.text: Je ne sais pas. Tu es une femme, vous avez le même âge.
examples.trans: I don't know. You're a woman, you're the same age.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.
for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
for a group of men, or a mixed group; elles for women only

examples.text: La gestion d'image pour les acteurs.
Et un pôle gestion d'image pour les acteurs.
examples.trans: And an image-management department for the actors.

examples.text: Noémie! Je parle d'image, pas de buzz.
examples.trans: Noemie! I am talking about image, not buzz.

meanings.note: Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: before the verb: vous la connaissez? les voilà
in speech: elle est là = she's here; je suis là = I'm here

examples.text: Je veux, mais je ne peux pas.
examples.trans: I want to, but I can't.

meanings.note: object pronoun before the verb: tu me donnes
with reflexive verbs: je me débrouille

meanings.note: moins de trente ans = under thirty

examples.trans: To appoint a new managing director.

examples.text: Il faudrait qu'il nomme un DG.
examples.trans: He should appoint a Managing Director.
I am nominated for the Cesars?

meanings.note: before the noun; nouvel before a vowel

meanings.note: everyday speech, with a he/she verb form

examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: tu vas où?; d'où = from where
